Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps (Redwood vs Bedrock/OpenAI)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sarah — really appreciate the candid feedback from your ML and platform teams. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum for the POC/competitive eval: 

- Key takeaways from discovery: primary workload is patient-facing summarization and triage routing (~4k daily requests, 300 token average). Data residency and audit logs are blockers for procurement.
- Your evaluation asks: 1) latency & cost comparison vs AWS Bedrock/OpenAI on your sample prompts, 2) hallucination/regression checks on clinical QA prompts, 3) controls for data separation and logging.

Proposed next steps:
1) Shared eval prompts: I attached a starter set (redwood-eval-prompts.csv) — please add any clinical prompts you want included.
2) Redwood will run a side-by-side on our dedicated infra (match 8xA100-equivalent) and return a token-cost/latency table + hallucination metrics.
3) Security: we'll provide SOC2 summary + proposed MUP language for legal (attached acme-mup-v1.pdf).
4) SE touchpoint: looping in Dev Patel (cc) to scope model-specific tests and timelines.

Can you confirm the list of prompts and whether procurement needs our standard AML/BAA docs up front? If you can share a short prioritized prompt list by Friday we’ll schedule the 48–72h run.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + next steps (Redwood vs Bedrock/OpenAI) — SE scope

Thanks for the context — quick proposal for the eval plan (high level):
1) Test matrix:
   - Prompt buckets: clinical QA (150 prompts), triage summarization (100 prompts), hallucination stress tests (50 adversarial prompts).
   - Models to run: Redwood-dedicated (rwd-13b/q8), OpenAI gpt-4o-mini, AWS Bedrock (tuned variant), Anthropic Claude-instant.
   - Modes: streaming vs non-streaming; KV cache enabled/disabled.

2) Metrics and outputs:
   - Latency (p50/p95) and per-token cost estimate (USD) normalized to Acme's volume.
   - Hallucination scoring: automated entailment check + manual spot review for high-confidence wrong outputs. We will flag hallucinations and provide 5 reproducible counterexamples per model.
   - Regression checks: compare against your historical golden outputs (if you provide) and compute BLEU/ROUGE where applicable + semantic similarity drop.

3) Timeline & resources:
   - If Acme finalizes prompt list by EOD Friday (Mar 6), we can run the 48–72h batch starting Mon. Estimated infra cost: ~$5k for the full matrix (we can absorb part for eval).

Attached: eval-results-template.xlsx (format for returned results).

Questions for Sarah: can you provide a 10–15 example golden set for regression checks? Also confirm whether PHI will be used in prompts — if so we need the BAA signed before running on customer data in Redwood Private.

Dev

- Regarding KV cache: we can run cache-disabled tests to emulate stateless endpoints for parity with Bedrock. That will increase latency/cost; we'll include both cache-on and cache-off rows in the results.

Lauren — based on the ask (multi-model side-by-side + manual spot checks), can we approve an extended 30-day trial and a promotional credit to help Acme run the matrix? I suggest a $10k eval credit and SE time to help with analysis.
